terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase, which he gives under “airline”: trāmes is a cross-way or path, and in the poets a course or flight (Lewis & Short), so the phrase names the route, not the company (see airline). Written with āë- as in āëroplanum.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 215, 270.
